headline: Custom Braces Save Three-Month-Old Panda's Ability to Eat
meta_description: Veterinarians created a custom orthodontic device to correct a three-month-old giant panda's misaligned jaw after injury prevented chewing and nursing.
summary_short: A three-month-old giant panda received a custom-made orthodontic appliance to correct a jaw deviation caused by injury, restoring its ability to eat and nurse.
body:
A three-month-old giant panda has received a custom orthodontic appliance to correct a mandibular deviation caused by injury. The young panda's jaw had been deviating to the side, making it impossible to chew or suckle—a critical concern at such a vulnerable age.

The specialized device was designed specifically for the panda's unique anatomy, representing a rare intersection of pediatric orthodontics and wildlife medicine. By addressing the misalignment, veterinarians have restored the panda's essential feeding functions, giving the cub a chance to nurse properly and develop normally.

This intervention underscores the lengths modern veterinary medicine will go to save endangered species. Giant pandas remain vulnerable, and every individual counts toward population recovery. The custom appliance offers hope that even severe injuries need not be fatal for young animals in professional care.
quick_facts: Three-month-old giant panda received custom orthodontic device
Jaw deviation prevented chewing and nursing after injury
Custom appliance restored panda's feeding ability
